facts: The Jaibos won the first league title in club history on April 5, 2026, beating Delfines de Puerto Vallarta 4 games to 2. The clincher went to extra innings, 10-7, in Vallarta.
It was their second straight trip to the final. A year earlier, Tabaqueros de Santiago beat them 4 games to 2. This time they knocked out Coqueros de Tuxpan 4-2 in the semis and finished the job.
A jaiba is a crab. The Jaibos are Sayulita's crabs, and the kids' team is the Jaibitos.
Baseball in Sayulita goes back to at least the 1970s. The club is run by volunteers and community donations.
Home is Estadio Manuel Rodríguez Sánchez on the north side of town. Sunday afternoon games are a tradition.
The league is the Liga Nayarita de Béisbol "Germán Jiménez Camarena", a winter league founded in 2000 for Nayarit-born players plus a few veterans.
Playoff series are best of seven. Six teams make the playoffs.
The league is named for Germán Jiménez Camarena, a lefty from Santiago Ixcuintla, Nayarit, who pitched for the Atlanta Braves in 1988. His only big-league win came against the Mets at Shea Stadium.
The Bahía de Banderas municipality pays for the team's bus rides to away games.
Want pro ball too? Jaguares de Nayarit play in the Mexican Pacific League in Tepic, which opens its season in mid-October.

news.headline: The league presented the 2026-27 season in Tepic with nine teams: Acaponeta, Compostela, Puerto Vallarta, Rosamorada, Santiago, Sayulita, Tecuala, Tuxpan and Ocelotes UAN.
The league says the regular season starts Nov 14 and lasts 9 weekends.
Pitcher Donnet Zamudio, described by the team as its historic strikeout leader, returns after an injury kept him out last season.
Starting pitcher Kender Villegas rejoins the Jaibos as a reinforcement for 2026-27 after being a key part of last season's rotation.
The Jaibos say they begin their title defense Saturday in Puerto Vallarta against Delfines.
The team released its 2026-27 schedule as an image, with the first home game on Sunday Nov 15 and home games at 1:00 p.m.
The league published the full 2026-27 rol de juegos as an image carousel.
Delfines announced the 2026-27 season would start Nov 13, a date the league's later posts moved to Nov 14.

town_facts: Magdalena is famous for fire opals, and the hills around it hold hundreds of opal and obsidian mines. Gem shops line the town.
It sits about 78 km northwest of Guadalajara, right next door to the town of Tequila.
Laguna de Magdalena, a big reservoir west of town, draws many bird species.
Magdalena (Jalisco).record: Not a LINABE team. No league record or 2025-26 result found.

Delfines de Puerto Vallarta.nickname: Delfines means dolphins, a nod to the dolphins of Banderas Bay.
town_facts: Puerto Vallarta became world famous after John Huston filmed The Night of the Iguana nearby in 1963.
The Malecón seaside boardwalk is lined with bronze sculptures.
It is the only Jalisco club in a Nayarit league. The Ameca River is the state line, and Sayulita sits just across it.
Delfines de Puerto Vallarta.record: 2025-26: second in the regular season, beat Ocelotes UAN in the quarterfinal and Tecuala 4-1 in the semifinal, then lost the final 4-2 to the Jaibos. No league title found. This is Sayulita's fiercest rivalry: the 2026 final had a brawl with 10 ejections. Split two preseason games with LMP club Charros de Jalisco on Oct 3-4, 2026. Manager: Osiris García.

Coqueros de Tuxpan.nickname: Coqueros means coconut growers or coconut sellers, a common trade on the Nayarit coast.
town_facts: Tuxpan is the smallest municipality in Nayarit, on rich farmland along the Río San Pedro.
Farmers here formed a land cooperative in 1919 that is described as one of the biggest in Mexico.
The Convent of Santa Catalina dates from 1607, and the Coamiles ceremonial site has about 40 known structures.
Coqueros de Tuxpan.record: A league power with 5 titles, including 2020-21, 2022-23 and 2023-24. 2025-26: third in the regular season, beat archrival Santiago in the quarterfinal, then lost the semifinal 4-2 to the Jaibos after leading 2-1.

hitters.name: Fernando Alaniz

hitters.name: Sergio Villalobos

hitters.name: Irving López

Tabaqueros de Santiago.nickname: Tabaqueros means tobacco growers. Santiago is one of the most important tobacco regions in Mexico.
town_facts: The municipality includes Mexcaltitán, an island village reachable only by boat, which local tradition links to Aztlán, the legendary homeland of the Aztecs.
The Nuestras Raíces mosaic mural covers about 1,100 square meters and tells the story of Mexico's origins.
Farms here grow tobacco, beans, watermelon, mangoes and chiles.
Tabaqueros de Santiago.record: The league's winningest club with 7 titles listed, most recently 2024-25, when they beat the Jaibos 4-1 in Game 6 of the final. 2025-26: fourth in the regular season, lost the quarterfinal to archrival Tuxpan.

hitters.name: Iván "El Foco" Morales
hitters.line: Game-tying HR plus a 2-run single in the 4-1 title clincher over Sayulita, March 2025.

hitters.name: Mauricio Ledezma
hitters.line: Walk-off hit in the 9th to beat Ocelotes UAN 2-1, Dec 2025.

hitters.name: Bryan Durán Langarica
hitters.line: Complete game in the 2024-25 clincher over Sayulita. Note: a Brian Durán Langarica pitched for Tuxpan in the 2026 semifinal.

Camaroneros de Tecuala.nickname: Camaroneros means shrimpers. Tecuala's lagoons, like Agua Brava, are big shrimp producers.
town_facts: Playa Novillero runs about 82 km and is billed as one of the longest beaches in the world.
Much of the west of the municipality is mangrove swamp inside the Marismas Nacionales reserve.
The name is said to mean a place of many wild animals.
Camaroneros de Tecuala.record: 1 title (2000). Sat out 2024-25 and returned for 2025-26. Finished sixth, lost the quarterfinal to the Jaibos but advanced as best loser, then lost the semifinal 4-1 to Puerto Vallarta.
Camaroneros de Tecuala.park: Estadio Santos Ramos Contreras (2026 playoff home games were played at Martín M. Sáizar in Acaponeta)

hitters.name: Javier Regla
hitters.line: Winning pitcher in a 17-7 semifinal win over Puerto Vallarta, March 2026.

town_facts: The name blends Tepehuano and Nahuatl words, roughly a place by the river where beans tangle in the reeds.
The town has one of Mexico's oldest corn flour plants and several mango packing houses.
Poet Alí Chumacero was born here.
Cachorros de Acaponeta.record: 3 titles: 2012-13, 2014-15 and 2019-20. Missed the six-team playoff field in 2025-26. Beat Compostela 15-1 in Dec 2025.

hitters.name: Gabriel Salas
hitters.line: Winning pitcher in a 15-1 win over Compostela, Dec 2025.

Pureros de Compostela.nickname: Pureros means cigar makers, from puro, Spanish for cigar. Nayarit is Mexico's main tobacco state.
town_facts: Founded in 1530 by conquistador Nuño de Guzmán and named after Santiago de Compostela in Spain.
The municipality includes the beach towns of Rincón de Guayabitos and La Peñita de Jaltemba, just up the coast from Sayulita.
It is the closest Nayarit rival to Sayulita by road.
Pureros de Compostela.record: 3 titles: 2001, 2004 and 2007-08. Missed the six-team playoff field in 2025-26. Lost 15-1 to Acaponeta in Dec 2025.

Ocelotes UAN.nickname: Ocelotes are ocelots, the spotted wild cat that is the mascot of the Universidad Autónoma de Nayarit (UAN).
town_facts: Tepic is the state capital, home of the state university that runs the team.
The city sits inland at about 900 meters, cooler than the coast.
Tepic's Coloso del Pacífico stadium hosts the pro Jaguares de Nayarit and hosted the 2026 LINABE All-Star Game.
Ocelotes UAN.record: 4 titles as the Diablos Rojos Universitarios de Tepic (2005, 2006, 2008-09, 2013-14). 2025-26: fifth in the regular season, lost the quarterfinal to Puerto Vallarta.

town_facts: Rosamorada means purple rose, after a tree with purple flowers that once stood in the town center.
Lagoons near the Pacific support fishing and shrimp farming, while the east rises toward the Sierra Madre.
Farms grow beans, chiles, rice, melons and watermelon.
Vaqueros de Rosamorada.record: 1 title (2018-19). Missed the six-team playoff field in 2025-26. Lost 16-5 to Tuxpan on opening day under new manager Antonio Lamas.
Vaqueros de Rosamorada.park: Estadio Pablo Zermeño Lamas (Wikipedia lists Carmelo Cervantes)

Tiburones de San Blas.nickname: Tiburones means sharks, fitting for an old Pacific port town.
town_facts: Founded in 1768 as Spain's launch port for expeditions to California. A 1760 fort with carvings of Spanish kings still stands on the hill.
Longfellow's last poem, The Bells of San Blas, was inspired by the bells of its ruined church.
Boats tour the mangroves of La Tovara, and birders have counted up to 292 species in a single Christmas Bird Count.
Tiburones de San Blas.record: Joined the league in 2023. Listed as a tentative entry for 2025-26 but not in the nine-team field that played. No results or titles found.
